cards.card: In this Protections example, the N-Boc methyl ester COC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)c1ccccc1C maps to di-tert-butyl dicarbonate plus the corresponding [NH3+] ester, COC(=O)[C@@H]([NH3+])c1ccccc1C. The methyl ester, stereochemistry, and o-methylphenyl group are retained.

For the C–C bond-formation example, the input Clc1ncncc1C#Cc1ccccc1 is disconnected at the heteroaryl–alkyne C–C bond. The correct output is phenylacetylene (C#Cc1ccccc1) plus the iodinated chloro-diazine (Clc1ncncc1I).

The input contains a phenolic –OH, while the correct output has –OCH₂Ph at that position; the rest of the scaffold is unchanged. Despite the “Deprotections” context label, preserve this specific O-benzylation transformation.

Despite the context label “Reductions,” the correct output converts the aryl –NH₂ in COc1cc(N)ccc1Oc1ccc(Cl)c(Cl)c1 to –[N⁺](=O)[O⁻]. The methoxy group, diaryl ether linkage, and both chlorines are retained.

The input has an N–CH₂CH₂OH substituent; the correct output has N–CH₂CO₂H instead. The other shown scaffold features are retained. Despite the stated reaction context “Reductions,” this specific change is alcohol-to-carboxylic-acid oxidation.

Input has an N-CH₂-COOH substituent and a Boc-protected amine. The output converts the acid to N-CH₂-COOCH₂CH₃ while retaining the Boc group and ring stereochemistry; do not remove Boc despite the “Deprotections” context.

For the methyl- and chloro-substituted fused [nH] heterocycle with a saturated N-containing ring and .Cl, the target is Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1NN.Cl.O=C1CCNCC1: the substituted arylhydrazine, chloride, and piperidone.
Despite the context label “Oxidations,” the example converts the aldehyde (O=CH–cage) to a primary alcohol (HOCH₂–cage), preserving the cage connectivity. Output: OCC12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2

The N-aryl, methyl-substituted pyrrole gives a ring-opened 1,4-diketone, CC(=O)CCC(=O)Ar, plus the benzoate with the pyrrole N-attachment restored as NH₂. Retain Ar’s Br and benzyloxy-F substituents, and retain the benzoate’s CO₂Me and NHAc groups. Although the context says heterocycle formation, the specified products show pyrrole cleavage.
The aryl–CH2Br substituent becomes aryl–CH3. The phenyl/chloro azaarene, amide, and stereodefined cyclohexylethyl group are retained; the output also includes N-bromosuccinimide.
FGI evidence: the substrate’s terminal ring-bound primary amine, [C@H]1N, becomes an azide, [C@H]1N=[N+]=[N-]. The rest of the scaffold and its specified stereochemistry remain unchanged.

Heteroatom arylation disconnection: the input’s pyrazole–N(pyrrolidine) bond is separated, giving CC1CCCN1 and the chlorinated pyrazole carboxamide. Preserve the pyrazole N-phenyl group and cage amide; the pyrazole carbon formerly bonded to pyrrolidine bears Cl in the product.

FGA example: the input is a dimethyl phosphate bearing an alkene and an allylic bromide (P–CH=CH–CH₂Br). The correct output is the rearranged alkene phosphate, C/C=C\P(=O)(OC)OC, together with N-bromosuccinimide, O=C1CCC(=O)N1Br.

The aryl–C(=O)–N(cyclic urea) bond is cleaved: the aryl carbonyl becomes –C(=O)OH, while the Boc-protected N-methyl benzyl substituent remains intact. The detached ring fragment is O=C1CNc2ccccc2N1; do not remove the Boc group.
Input contains an N-methyl cyclic imide; the correct output replaces n(C) with [nH] and includes CI as a separate component. Preserve the methoxy groups and fused-ring framework.
The input has a phenolic OH, while the correct output has OCH₃ at that position; the rest of the structure is unchanged. This is methylation, despite the “Deprotections” context label.
